source_text: In Lazarum Ἀμφιλοχίου ἐπισκόπου Ἰκονίου λόγος εἰς τὸν τετραήμερον Λάζαρον Φέρε πάλιν εἰς μέσον τὸν εὐαγγελιστὴν Ἰωάννην· καλὸν γὰρ τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τῆς ἀναστάσεως σκοπῆσαι. Ἤκουες γὰρ αὐτοῦ ἀρτίως λέγοντος· Πρὸ ἓξ ἡμερῶν τοῦ Πάσχα ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς βηθανίαν, ὅπου ἦν Λάζαρος, ὃν ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν. Εἶδες τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐν Λαζάρῳ προτυπωθεῖσαν, ἣν ὁ πιστὸς ὄχλος ἐγνώρισεν; Οἱ ὄχλοι ἐγνώρισαν καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐλοιδόρησαν τὴν θαυματουργίαν εἰς βασκανίαν μεταβαλόντες. Ὄντως ἐβάσκαναν τὴν ἀνάστασιν Λαζάρου, ὅτι μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν αὐτοῦ, ἣν ἤκουες, συνεβουλεύσαντο αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι. Εἶδες βασκανίας ὑπερβολήν; Ὃν ὁ κύριος ἤγειρεν, αὐτοὶ ἀποκτεῖναι διενοήθησαν, μὴ συνειδότες ὅτι κἂν αὐτοὶ ἀποκτείνω σι, πάλιν κοῦφον τῷ κυρίῳ ἀναστῆσαι τὸν φίλον. Συνεβουλεύσαντο τὸν Λάζαρον ἀποκτεῖναι· οὐδὲν οὕτως ἐδρίμυττε τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ὡς ἡ ἀνάστασις τοῦ Λαζάρου. Τοῦτο μόνον τὸ θαῦμα οὐκ ἴσχυσαν συκοφαντῆσαι. Τὴν ἀνάβλεψιν τοῦ ἐκ γεννητῆς τυφλοῦ ἐσυκοφάντησαν λέγοντες· Οὗτός ἐστιν· οὐκ ἔστιν οὗτος· ὅμοιος αὐτοῦ ἐστιν. Τὴν ἔγερσιν τῆς θυγατρὸς Ἰαήρου ἐσυκο φάντησαν λέγοντες ὡς κατηνέχθη καὶ οὐ τελείῳ θανάτῳ παρεδόθη. Τὴν ἀνάστασιν τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς χήρας τοῦ μονογενοῦς ἐσυκοφάντησαν λέγοντες ὡς τὸν θάνατον ἐσχηματίσατο καὶ οὐχ ὑπὸ τῆς τυραννίδος τοῦ θανάτου κατεπόθη. Τὴν ξηρανθεῖσαν συκῆν ἐσυκοφάντησαν λέγοντες ὡς τρυγωνισθεῖσαν καὶ οὐχ ὡς δεσποτικῷ ῥήματι ξηρανθεῖσαν. Τὴν τοῦ ὕδατος εἰς οἶνον μεταβολὴν ἐσυκοφάντησαν λέγοντες ὡς ἤδη τῶν ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ μεθυσθέντων καὶ μὴ εἰδότων τὴν χλεύην. Τὴν ἀνάστασιν μόνην τοῦ Λαζάρου οὐκ ἴσχυσαν συκοφαντῆσαι. Ἤδεισαν τὸν Λάζαρον· ἐπίσημος ἦν ὁ ἀνήρ. Ἠκολούθησαν τῇ κηδίᾳ, εἶδον τὸν τάφον σφραγιζόμενον, παρεμυθήσαντο κατὰ τὸ εἰωθός, ὡς ἐν περιδείπ νῳ θανάτου, Μάρθαν καὶ Μαρίαν τὰς ἀδελφὰς Λαζάρου. Ἔγνωσαν ὅτι τέσσαρας ἡμέρας εἶχεν ἀκριβῶς ἐν τῷ μνημείῳ κατατεθείς, καὶ ὅτι τετραήμερος νεκρὸς πάντοθεν ἔξαρθρος, τῶν σαρκῶν μειωθέντων, τῶν ὀστέων ἐκγομφωθέντων, τῆς νευροστασίας διασπασθείσης, τῶν ἐνδοσθίων σκορπισθέντων, τῆς γαστρὸς ἐκχυθείσης. Ταῦτα συνειδότες ὡς εἶδον ἀθρόον τὴν ἀνάστασιν Λαζάρου σῶαν, ἀρτίαν ὡς ἀπὸ τόρνου, στίλβουσαν τῇ παλινβιωσίᾳ, ἐταράχθησαν. Μικροῦ δεῖν ἀπέψυξαν μὴ εὑρίσκον τες λόγους προφασιλογίας, τὸ πῶς συκοφαντήσουσι τὴν ἀνάστασιν Λαζάρου τῆς τοῦ κυρίου πραγματείας τοῦτο κατα σκευασάσης. Τί ἐστι, τῆς τοῦ κυρίου πραγματείας τοῦτο παρασκευα σάσης; Ἄκουε διὰ βραχέων.
orientation: Amphilochius opens his homily by calling the congregation to look again at John's account of Lazarus, the firstfruits of the resurrection, and shows how the Jewish leaders could slander every other miracle but not this one.
pass_a_gloss: On Lazarus. Of Amphilochius bishop of Iconium, a discourse on the four-days-dead Lazarus. Bring again into the midst the evangelist John; for it is good to contemplate the firstfruits of the resurrection. For you were hearing him just now saying: Six days before the Passover Jesus came into Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom he raised from the dead. Did you see the firstfruits of the resurrection prefigured in Lazarus, which the faithful crowd recognized? The crowds recognized it and the chief priests reviled the wonder-working, turning it into envy. Truly they envied the resurrection of Lazarus, because after his resurrection, which you were hearing, they plotted to kill him. Did you see the excess of envy? The one whom the Lord raised, they intended to kill, not knowing that even if they kill him, again it is easy for the Lord to raise the friend. They plotted to kill Lazarus; nothing so stung the Jews as the resurrection of Lazarus. This miracle alone they were not able to slander. The giving of sight to the man blind from birth they slandered, saying: This is he; this is not he; he is like him. The raising of the daughter of Jairus they slandered, saying that she had fallen into a deep sleep and was not handed over to complete death. The resurrection of the only son of the widow they slandered, saying that he feigned death and was not swallowed by the tyranny of death. The withered fig tree they slandered, saying that it had been stripped by grape-gatherers and not withered by the master's word. The change of water into wine they slandered, saying that those at the dinner were already drunk and did not know the trick. The resurrection alone of Lazarus they were not able to slander. They knew Lazarus; the man was well known. They followed the funeral, they saw the tomb being sealed, they consoled according to custom, as at a funeral feast of death, Martha and Mary the sisters of Lazarus. They knew that he had been exactly four days laid in the tomb, and that a four-days-dead corpse was wholly disjointed, the flesh wasted away, the bones loosened from their sockets, the sinew-binding torn apart, the inward parts scattered, the belly poured out. Knowing these things, when they saw suddenly the resurrection of Lazarus sound, complete as from a lathe, gleaming with renewed life, they were troubled. They all but fainted, not finding words of pretext, how they might slander the resurrection of Lazarus, since the strategy of the Lord had prepared this. What is it, since the strategy of the Lord had prepared this? Hear in brief.

choices.why: Glossary requires firstfruits for ἀπαρχή and resurrection for ἀνάστασις; the phrase is the homily's central image of Lazarus as the initial pledge.
Glossary requires envy for βασκανία; the chief priests' reviling is characterized as malicious envy, not mere malice.
Glossary requires slander for συκοφαντέω; the verb describes misrepresenting miracles with false explanations.
Glossary requires four days dead for τετραήμερος; the title and repeated emphasis stress the certainty of Lazarus' death.
Glossary requires strategy for πραγματεία; Jesus' deliberate arrangement of events is the point of the passage.
The simile conveys the completeness and smoothness of the restored body; kept literal to preserve the image.

pass_b_english: Let us bring the evangelist John into our midst again, for it is good to contemplate the firstfruits of the resurrection. You heard him say just now: "Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom he had raised from the dead" (John 11:1). Did you see the firstfruits of the resurrection prefigured in Lazarus, which the faithful crowd recognized? The crowds recognized it, and the chief priests reviled the wonder-working, turning it into envy. They truly envied the resurrection of Lazarus, because after his resurrection, which you heard about, they plotted to kill him. Did you see the excess of envy? The one whom the Lord raised, they resolved to kill, not realizing that even if they killed him, it would again be easy for the Lord to raise his friend. They plotted to kill Lazarus. Nothing stung the Jews as much as the resurrection of Lazarus. This miracle alone they could not slander. They slandered the healing of the man born blind, saying, "This is he; no, it is not he; it is someone like him" (John 9:9). They slandered the raising of Jairus's daughter, saying that she had merely collapsed and had not been handed over to complete death. They slandered the resurrection of the widow's only son, saying that he had feigned death and had not been swallowed up by the tyranny of death. They slandered the withered fig tree, saying that it had been stripped by birds and not withered by the Lord's word. They slandered the changing of water into wine, saying that the dinner guests were already drunk and did not recognize the jest. Only the resurrection of Lazarus they could not slander. They knew Lazarus; the man was well known. They had followed the funeral procession, they had seen the tomb being sealed, they had consoled Martha and Mary, the sisters of Lazarus, according to custom, as at a funeral meal for the dead. They knew that he had lain in the tomb for exactly four days, and that he was a corpse four days dead, completely disjointed, his flesh wasted away, his bones loosened from their sockets, his sinews torn apart, his inward parts scattered, his belly dissolved. Knowing all this, when they suddenly saw the resurrection of Lazarus whole and complete, as from a lathe, gleaming with renewed life, they were thrown into confusion. They nearly fainted, finding no words of pretext for how they might slander the resurrection of Lazarus, since the Lord's strategy had arranged this. What does it mean that the Lord's strategy had arranged this? Listen briefly.
notes: OCR damage in several places: 'ἀποκτείνω σι' likely ἀποκτείνωσι; 'ἐσυκο φάντησαν' likely ἐσυκοφάντησαν; 'περιδείπ νῳ' likely περιδείπνῳ; 'εὑρίσκον τες' likely εὑρίσκοντες; 'κατα σκευασάσης' likely κατασκευασάσης; 'παρασκευα σάσης' likely παρασκευασάσης. Gloss reflects the evident intended readings.

problems.why: The passage is from John 11, not John 12:1.
problems.ruling: Greek quotes John 12:1 verbatim, but John 12:1 does contain these exact words; however, the claim says John 11. Checking: John 12:1 reads 'Πρὸ ἓξ ἡμερῶν τοῦ πάσχα ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Βηθανίαν...' — the citation John 12:1 is actually correct, not John 11. The reported problem is wrong; the citation is accurate.

problems.why: Reader may think 'monument' is a separate structure, not the tomb.
Lazarus emerging smooth and shaped like woodwork is bizarre; likely means 'renewed, perfected' or 'as if newly created'.
problems.fix: Consider 'as if newly fashioned' or note lathe as image of craftsmanship.

problems.quote: "Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom he had raised from the dead" (John 11:1)
problems.why: John 11:1 says 'Lazarus of Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha'—'six days before Passover' is John 12:1.
problems.fix: Correct to '(John 12:1)' or note conflation of passages.

problems.quote: "This is he; no, it is not he; it is someone like him" (John 9:9)
problems.why: John 9:9 has the man born blind speaking, not the Jews slandering; they question in 9:8-9, but 'slandered' misattributes motive and compresses dialogue.
problems.fix: Note: 'the neighbors disputed' (John 9:8) rather than 'they slandered'.

problems.quote: the resurrection of the widow's only son
problems.why: 'Raising' and 'resurrection' used interchangeably for the same category of miracle.
problems.fix: Use 'raising' for all three miracles, reserve 'resurrection' for Lazarus.

problems.why: 'As from a lathe' is an opaque simile; a lathe produces smoothness but the image is unclear here.
problems.fix: Render as 'as if newly shaped' or 'as if freshly formed.'

problems.why: John 11:1 says 'Now a certain man was ill, Lazarus of Bethany.' The quoted words match John 12:1.

last_rejected.why: προφασιλογία means 'making excuses/pretexts', but 'words of pretext' is awkward; 'excuses' or 'pretexts' better.

last_rejected.why: κατασκευάσασης means 'prepared/constructed/arranged', but context suggests 'contrived' or 'devised' with sense of deliberate planning; 'arranged' is weak.
last_rejected.fix: since the Lord's strategy had prepared this

last_rejected.quote: They slandered the raising of Jairus's daughter, saying that she had merely collapsed and had not been handed over to complete death.
last_rejected.source_quote: Τὴν ἔγερσιν τῆς θυγατρὸς Ἰαήρου ἐσυκοφάντησαν λέγοντες ὡς κατηνέχθη καὶ οὐ τελείῳ θανάτῳ παρεδόθη.
last_rejected.why: Greek κατηνέχθη means ‘was seized/held’, not ‘collapsed’. The English misrepresents the accusation.
last_rejected.fix: They slandered the raising of Jairus's daughter, saying that she had been seized and not handed over to complete death.
last_rejected.ruling: κατηνέχθη is passive of κατάγω, 'bring down'; 'collapsed' is within normal semantic range for a girl 'brought down' by illness/death.
